Match its warm ivory paper background, deep forest-green elegant serif headings, restrained muted blue/orange/green accents, crisp generous spacing, photographic or convincingly realistic tiny subject illustrations where relevant, subtle dimensional feature-map cards. Large readable labels. Original layout for this brief. No watermarks. Wide 3:2 or 16:10 composition, use minimal text and large clear arrows; all text inside frame. Conceptual not fabricated experimental evidence. An RNN Unrolled Over Time.* A horizontal diagram on a white background with three identical blue rounded boxes in a row, each labelled "RNN cell (same weights)". Below each box, an upward arrow from a word token: "dog", "bites", "man", labelled x₁, x₂, x₃. Between the boxes, rightward orange arrows labelled h₁ and h₂, and a final orange arrow leaving the third box labelled h₃ "final hidden state: a summary of the whole sentence". On the far left, a small grey circle feeding the first box labelled "h₀ = zeros". Above the diagram, a curved bracket spanning all three boxes labelled "one cell, applied once per step". Takeaway: an RNN reads in order, passing its memory forward from step to step.
ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS OVERRIDE CONFLICTING WORDING: Use exact dimensions and correct math. Label schematic where appropriate.

brief: The LSTM's Memory Lane.* A single wide LSTM cell drawn as a rounded rectangle on a white background. Across the top runs a thick straight horizontal green line labelled "cell state (long-term memory)", entering on the left as c(t−1) and leaving on the right as c(t). On this line sit two small circles: a "×" circle fed from below by a small gate box labelled "forget gate f (0–1)", and a "+" circle fed from below by a box labelled "input gate × new candidate". Lower in the cell, a thinner orange line carries the hidden state h(t−1) in from the left and h(t) out on the right, with a box labelled "output gate" connecting the cell state down to h(t). The current input x(t) enters from the bottom and feeds all three gate boxes. A callout beside the green line: "if f ≈ 1, memory and gradient flow straight through". Takeaway: the LSTM keeps a protected memory line that gates can preserve across many steps.

brief: Chain vs. Direct Access.* Two horizontal panels on a white background, each with the same six word boxes in a row: "The", "film", "…", "…", "director", "was". Top panel titled "RNN: information travels along a chain": orange arrows link each box to the next, left to right, and a long faint red arrow underneath points from "was" back to "film", labelled "signal must pass through every step in between". Bottom panel titled "Attention: every word can look at every word": from "was", six curved blue lines of different thickness fan out to all six boxes, with the line to "film" drawn thickest and labelled "high weight", and the lines to "…" thin, labelled "low weight". Caption beneath the bottom panel: "distance doesn't matter; relevance does". Takeaway: attention replaces a long chain of steps with direct, weighted connections.

brief: How to Read a 2D Picture of a Representation.* A three-column comparison card on a white background. Column 1, "Full representation (64 numbers)": a small cube filled with coloured point clouds, labelled "the truth: measure here". Column 2, "PCA (a shadow)": a light source casting the cube's shadow onto a wall, producing overlapping coloured blobs; a tag below reads "keeps: big directions of spread · loses: many neighbourhoods". Column 3, "t-SNE (a rearrangement)": the same coloured clouds pulled apart into neat separate islands on a flat sheet, with dashed arrows showing islands that could be swapped in position; a tag below reads "keeps: who is next to whom · loses: distances between islands".
